stem: Which feature most strongly distinguishes malignant hyperthermia from environmental heat illness?

options.A: It is a hypermetabolic crisis triggered by certain anesthetic agents, including volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine, in susceptible individuals.
options.B: It occurs only after prolonged exposure to hot environmental temperatures.
options.C: It develops gradually over months as a chronic metabolic disease.
options.D: It requires strenuous exercise in hot conditions as the triggering event.

rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited susceptibility in which exposure to triggering anesthetic agents—classically potent volatile inhalational anesthetics and succinylcholine—can produce an acute hypermetabolic crisis. Environmental heat exposure or exertion is not required. A is correct.
educational_objective: Identify anesthetic-triggered susceptibility as a defining feature of malignant hyperthermia.
source_organization: Malignant Hyperthermia Association of the United States (MHAUS)

source_claim_supported: Malignant hyperthermia occurs in susceptible individuals and is triggered by potent volatile inhalational anesthetics and/or succinylcholine.

source_original.stem: A nurse is distinguishing between malignant hyperthermia and heat stroke. The key distinguishing feature of malignant hyperthermia is that it:

options.A: A pharmacogenetic crisis triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine in susceptible people
options.B: A heat illness caused only by prolonged environmental exposure without any anesthetic trigger
options.C: A chronic metabolic disorder that develops gradually over months rather than during anesthesia
options.D: An exertional heat illness caused by exercise in hot conditions rather than anesthetic exposure

source_original.rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is specifically triggered by certain anesthetic agents (such as succinylcholine or volatile inhaled anesthetics) in genetically susceptible individuals, typically occurring acutely during or shortly after surgical anesthesia — distinct from heat stroke, which results from environmental heat exposure and/or exertion, though both are hypermetabolic emergencies requiring rapid cooling and supportive treatment.
source_original.source_detail: MHAUS, What is MH / MHAUS and trigger-agent guidance; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed unnecessary heat-stroke treatment comparison, retained the MHAUS-supported trigger/susceptibility distinction, and reduced difficulty to medium.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Trigger agents and susceptibility directly supported.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked MHAUS trigger guidance; A remains unique.
